newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil off, low sulphur dips on oversupply.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil off, low sulphur dips on oversupply.

text.p: NWE gas oil weakened on Tuesday in line with strong losses in benchmark IPE futures and ample supply amid lacklustre demand, traders said.
June IPE settled $4 lower at $170.00 a tonne.

Heating oil barges traded at June IPE +$1 and +$1.25 fob Rotterdam for first half June delivery mid afternoon, but premiums were quoted in a wide band ranging June IPE +0.75 cents/+$1.50 fob Rotterdam.
"It's very quiet," said one trader. "There's really nothing doing."
Low sulphur was under pressure as arbitraged Algerian and Italian cargoes flooded into the area amid fairly lacklustre demand.
One player appeared to be taking advantage of the drop in premiums picking up at least three cargoes throughout the day at June IPE +$6.0, $6.50 and $5.25 for first half delivery.
Some players speculated the buyer might be considering working the arb to the Far East which had reopened as NWE and Mediterranean prices tumbled.
A 25,000 tonne flexi-cargo was done to a different player at July IPE +$5.75 cif Le Havre for second half June delivery.
